Before procurement signs off we need two things: a clear per-token slab pricing schedule (including any commit-tier discounts and how overages are charged) and a CSV export of our last 3 months of per-endpoint token usage to reconcile against our internal cost model.

Quick background:
- We expect to start with ~30M input+output tokens/month and ramp to ~120M over six months.
- We use the streaming generate endpoint heavily for real-time assistants and separate batch embedding jobs for analytics.

Specific asks:
1) A proposed commit tiers table (monthly token thresholds -> % discount) and whether tiering mixes across endpoints or is per-model.
2) Exact invoice line-item mapping: what will appear as line items for a hosted usage invoice (tokens, storage, ephemeral GPU time, reserved credits, etc.).
3) A sample CSV export (token-level breakdown by endpoint/date) we can import into our cost model.

We have a procurement call on Aug 12 — can we get those items by EOD Aug 9?

Thanks,

Hi team — looping in for billing detail and sample exports. Per your questions:

1) Invoice presentation for commits
- We present usage at list price with a separate line item for "Commit Discount / Reserved Credit" so auditors can reconcile easily. Example lines:
  - HOSTED USAGE (tokens) — 31,250,000 tokens @ $0.0008/token -> $25,000
  - COMMIT DISCOUNT (50M/month tier) -> -$5,000
  - RESERVED CAPACITY CREDIT -> -$2,000 (if reserved GPU capacity applied)
  - NET CHARGE -> $18,000

2) Line-item breakdown we will include in the CSV export
- date, endpoint, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, region, request_id (when available), feature_flag (streaming/batch), invoice_line_code

3) Overages
- Overages are billed at the slab rate that corresponds to the total consumption bucket for that billing period (so if you exceed a slab, the marginal tokens above the threshold get billed at the higher slab unless you have prepaid credits). We can alternatively arrange true-up invoices monthly with a separate overage invoice if procurement prefers.

4) Next steps
- Attached: sample-invoice-lineitems.csv (this shows a mock 3-month export and a mapping file).
- Rishi/Jordan: I can run a one-off export for Hemingway and push to the shared Drive link Rishi provided; confirm the Drive path and I’ll upload by COB Aug 9.

—Marissa
